Namaste, I'm Hema. You're watching This Day, That Year.
hema
Today's date is the fifth of October. And fifteen years ago, it was 2026.
hema
Old weather. The weather office forecast heavy rain over Kerala, Tamil Nadu and coastal Karnataka, while the monsoon began leaving parts of Maharashtra.
hema
We now schedule rain by subscription. Back then, it just arrived and nobody got a receipt.
hema
Old money. Gold crossed fourteen thousand rupees for a single gram, and the whole country checked its drawers.
hema
Today gold is cheap. We wear it to hide the price of chai.
hema
Vintage gadget. A screenless fitness band reached India. It tracked your sleep and showed you nothing, like a polite alarm clock.
hema
That's the record. Everything else is just a take. I'm Hema. Namaste, see you at the next bulletin.

Namaskara! Meter down. Tchu Tchu reporting, live from the taxi.
tchu
The weather office says rain in the south, so my passengers carry umbrellas for a shower that is a thousand kilometres away. Optimists.
tchu
A woman asked the price of gold per gram, then asked the fare per kilometre. Same face. The meter ran.
tchu
Fa King Construction has stuck a third notice at Celeb Shauchalay. The poster is still crooked. Who notices a notice?
tchu
Tchu Tchu, AIMTV, Bombai. The meter is still running.
sarla
Hi guys! It's Stomach Challo, and today I have left the country again. Passport not needed, only a full tank. I love foreign.
sarla
Okay, it is Lonavala. But the chikki here is so Swiss. Every piece has been through at least one hill station.
sarla
The monsoon is leaving this part of Maharashtra, so the valley looks like a postcard that is still drying.
sarla
I took a selfie at the viewpoint. The valley photobombed me with fog. Very international of it.
sarla
The vada pav is practically a continental breakfast. Two carbs in a bun, very European.
sarla
That's it for today. Stay hungry, stay foreign. This is Stomach Challo, signing off from West India.
